name: Blood Pressure Grade 1 Hypertension
recommendedAction: Lifestyle modification with AAM visit in 2-4 weeks
escalationThreshold: 160/100 mmHg or symptoms of hypertensive urgency
targetPopulation: Adults with no prior CVD or diabetes
medicationConsideration: Defer unless high risk or additional risk factors

name: Blood Pressure Grade 2 Hypertension
recommendedAction: Lifestyle modification AND pharmacotherapy, urgent AAM visit
targetPopulation: All adults; mandatory medication for most
medicationConsideration: Initiate first-line antihypertensives (ACE-I, ARB, CCB, diuretic)

name: Hypertensive Urgency/Emergency
applicableCondition: BP >=180/>=120 mmHg with or without symptoms
recommendedAction: IMMEDIATE referral to emergency department or urgent care
medicationConsideration: May need IV antihypertensives in ED setting

name: Mild to Moderate Anemia
applicableCondition: Hemoglobin 7-12 g/dL in males, 7-11 g/dL in females
recommendedAction: Investigate cause, dietary modification, AAM visit within 2 weeks

name: Severe Anemia
recommendedAction: URGENT referral to specialist/hospital for evaluation and possible transfusion
medicationConsideration: May require transfusion, IV iron, or EPO

name: Prediabetes Management
recommendedAction: Intensive lifestyle modification, AAM visit every 3 months
escalationThreshold: Progression to diabetes or development of metabolic syndrome
targetPopulation: Adults with prediabetes, BMI >25, or significant risk factors
medicationConsideration: Metformin if high risk (age <60, BMI >35, family history)
efficacy: Lifestyle alone 58% effective; with metformin 71% effective at preventing diabetes

name: Diabetes Mellitus Management
applicableCondition: Fasting glucose >=126 mg/dL OR HbA1c >=6.5% OR symptoms + glucose >200 mg/dL
recommendedAction: Pharmacotherapy initiation, intensive lifestyle, AAM visit every 3 months

monitoringIntervals.lab_recheck: HbA1c every 3 months until <7%, then every 6 months

medicationConsideration: First-line: Metformin; add second agent if needed

name: Cardiac Monitoring Protocol
applicableCondition: History of MI, chest pain, arrhythmia, or high-risk presentation
recommendedAction: ECG, troponin testing, continuous monitoring if hospitalized
escalationThreshold: Recurrent chest pain, arrhythmia, or ECG changes
targetPopulation: Patients with known or suspected cardiac disease
medicationConsideration: Antiplatelet, beta-blocker, ACE-I, statin per standard protocols

name: Kidney Disease Monitoring
recommendedAction: Baseline staging, regular monitoring, specialist referral for Stage 4-5
escalationThreshold: GFR decline >5-10%, severe proteinuria, or potassium abnormality
medicationConsideration: ACE-I or ARB for proteinuria, BP control essential

name: Diabetic Eye Screening Protocol
recommendedAction: Referral to ophthalmology for comprehensive dilated exam annually
escalationThreshold: Any retinopathy findings or vision changes

monitoringIntervals.ophthalmology_exam: annually for diabetics with no retinopathy
monitoringIntervals.urgent_referral: if vision changes or macular edema suspected

medicationConsideration: Anti-VEGF or laser treatment if retinopathy present

name: Acute Stroke Protocol
applicableCondition: Acute neurological deficit with time of onset <4.5 hours
recommendedAction: IMMEDIATE emergency evaluation, possible thrombolytic therapy or thrombectomy
escalationThreshold: Any suspected stroke symptom requires emergency evaluation

monitoringIntervals.thrombectomy_window: up to 24 hours based on imaging

medicationConsideration: IV tPA if eligible; mechanical thrombectomy if large vessel occlusion
